big_case.notes: Interim stay, not a merits judgment, but the per curiam announces a categorical rule ('There is no such thing as a "constitutional" major-questions claim') that reaches every jurisdiction-stripping statute preserving only constitutional claims, and it unblocks border-barrier construction across the Big Bend Sector under IIRIRA s.102 waivers. High practical and doctrinal salience for an application; below a merits landmark.

leakage.notes: Forward cell; all logged calls dated 2026-10-29, eleven days before the 2026-11-09 disposition existed. Web/MCP retrieval was general authority (Dalton v. Specter, REAL ID Act text); no query for this application's status; no data/qp-topics access. Prose explicitly disclaims knowing the outcome.

central_claims.basis: Nov 9 order: application granted; injunction stayed pending the filing and disposition of a cert petition.
central_claims.claim: The Court will grant the government's application and stay the W.D. Tex. injunction pending a timely certiorari petition (80%).

central_claims.basis: Per curiam grants 'the requested stay'; no summary reversal entered.
central_claims.claim: A stay, not summary reversal on the alternative petition request, is the likely route.

central_claims.basis: Per curiam: the Government is 'exceedingly likely to prevail' that the District Court lacked jurisdiction; the claim 'alleges instead that the Secretary exceeded his statutory authority' (Dalton).
central_claims.claim: If explained, the ground will be the distinction between a genuinely constitutional claim and a claim that the Secretary exceeded statutory authority, via the s.102(c) jurisdictional limit rather than the full constitutional validity of the waiver scheme.

central_claims.basis: Docket Nov 9: application referred to the Court; order recites referral by Justice Alito.
central_claims.claim: The application will be referred to the full Court before disposition (95%).

central_claims.basis: Only a noted vote: 'JUSTICE JACKSON would deny'; no separate writing. The order was explained by a per curiam, not unexplained; claim was hedged.
central_claims.claim: A reasoned dissent is plausible, with Jackson and Sotomayor the most likely writers; an unexplained order with noted votes remains quite possible.
